claim: To make a wall or building look lower, give a strip of open ground in front of it (an apron) a lower parallax sky: the face is drawn only up to that sky.
evidence: the owner, 2026-11-17, walking the build in NBlood: 'when you put parallax sky low it is covering view like a normal ceiling'
projects/blood-city/experiments/church-roofs/before: the tower painted 0 px in yard_to_tower
use: Never lower a sky to shorten a face; skyline.lowered_skies finds one on a built map.
instead: The face is shorter but the low sky is a lid: it is painted from the far wall's top upward over every column the strip covers, so everything behind and above it (a tower set back, the blocks beyond) vanishes. Lower a thing by making it a sector whose floor is its top, under the common sky.

checked.how: Opened projects/blood-city/experiments/church-roofs/README.md: owner's words 'when you put parallax sky low it is covering view like a normal ceiling' (also hypothesis.json owner_said); before/ yard_to_tower: tower '17.4 bodies tall ... paints 0 pixels'; 'the renderer paints it from the top of the far wall upward over every column the sector covers'; raised-floor sectors replaced aprons. bloodmap/skyline.py:124 roof, :231 lowered_skies exist.
